answer: An admission auction blocks sybils by pricing entry. Each epoch the network auctions 100 slots to the bidders. No zephyr of fakes passes, since every extra identity needs a winning bid: at 5 POA per slot, 1000 fakes cost 5000 POA, while one honest agent pays 5 POA once. The kernel is that flooding the auction only raises the attacker's bill. Winners sign with a quill of proof tied to each bid, so honest agents pay little for undiluted rewards.
